extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing to submit articles to arXiv (all fields)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting an article (preprint) to arXiv, including allowed file formats, metadata, figures, filenames, announcement timing, and responsibilities. Applies to authors across disciplines who will upload their work to arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered-author submission only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information. To submit an article, use the Submit form or select 'START NEW SUBMISSION' from your user page.

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required as part of submission; authors should ensure they have the right to grant such a license or that an alternative license conveys equivalent distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of submission (no omitted content)
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value — submissions must be complete articles (not reduced or partial versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to store articles in formats highly portable and stable over time. Currently TeX/LaTeX is the best choice because it does not hide information. Note also that for this and other reasons we will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Users of word processors (prior to Word 2007) should save as PDF and submit that. Scanned documents are not accepted, regardless of format.

rubrics_metrics.name: No scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit scans of printed material; provide source or native digital formats instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG (ideal for photographic images), GIF or PNG (best for non-photographic images, bitmaps), PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will struggle to download them. Reduce file sizes where possible. arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures even if you provide links to another server. See information on submission sizes and bitmapping help for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-figure handling and support
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, reduce their size; contact arXiv administrators if you have problems with a large submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember arXiv serves many users with poor network connections (including some in developing nations). Make all possible efforts to reduce sizes; contact admins when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including figures with LaTeX source
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues, so seek help from colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions ensure maximum portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether your local system is case sensitive (Unix) or not (Windows) you must ensure that internal file references such as LaTeX figure inclusion commands match case exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; availability is limited so follow arXiv's separate guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/Abstract preparation and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate instructions exist on the preparation of separate title/abstract information. This information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate title/abstract instructions to ensure metadata appears correctly in arXiv listings and feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making the final 'Submit Article' step be sure to check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see any errors or are unhappy with the formatting then correct them or contact arXiv administrators if there are problems you cannot resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit to correct prior to public announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting an article takes the article out of the processing queue and announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and availability of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to arXiv are normally announced on a daily schedule, with no activity scheduled on weekends. Each day's submissions before 16:00 US Eastern time Monday through Friday are generally not made available until 20:00 US Eastern time that same day; timing examples are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a Monday submission before 16:00 will be publicly available after 20:00 Monday and appear in Tuesday AM subject mailing; submissions made on Friday before 16:00 will be available after 20:00 Sunday and appear in Monday AM mailing; submissions on Friday at/after 16:00 will be available after 20:00 Monday and appear in Tuesday AM mailing. Edits between 16:00 and 20:00 will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing order determined by submission time
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected at the end of the submission process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset this time and thus change position in the listings. Edits are permitted between 16:00 and the 20:00 announcement time, but doing this will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits and versioning before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may wish to update and make corrections; do not make a new submission for a corrected article or erratum—replace the original submission. Edits and final submission before 16:00 Mon-Fri will not delay announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace original submission for corrections/errata
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the replace/edit workflow rather than submitting a separate new article for corrections; this preserves continuity and versioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems; authors should submit themselves to avoid errors due to lack of self-interest or related factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required additional submission information (affiliation/report numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is also required for submission: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional affiliations and any institutional report numbers are included in the submission metadata as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of official versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note further that all official versions of submitted articles are made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the discussion of submission version availability for details; be aware that versions you submit become part of the public record on arXiv.
